rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes a controlled aging heat treatment to precipitate B2 nano-precipitates, while the target paper added 4.2 at.% Cr via vacuum arc melting to form a Laves phase. These are different kinds of interventions (heat treatment vs. composition change).
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies high-temperature testing around 1000°C under tensile/creep loading, whereas the target paper conducted room-temperature compression testing. These are contradictory regimes.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes precipitation strengthening via coherent B2 nano-precipitates and Orowan looping. The target paper describes a dual mechanism of solid solution hardening and crack hindrance by a reticulated Laves phase. These are different general classes of mechanism.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts increased high-temperature yield strength with unchanged room-temperature properties. The target paper reports a concurrent increase in room-temperature yield strength and fracture strain. The property direction is opposite (high-temperature vs. room-temperature improvement) and the specific outcome differs.
